candidates.name: Psoriasis
support_spans: well‐defined hyperpigmented, hyperkeratotic plaques with thick adherent scales
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of hyperkeratotic plaques with thick adherent scales and the biopsy findings of hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis are consistent with psoriasis.

candidates.name: Hypothyroidism-associated dermatitis
support_spans: thyroid‐stimulating hormone was elevated at 16.6 mIU/L
candidates.why: The elevated thyroid-stimulating hormone level suggests hypothyroidism, which can be associated with dermatitis.

candidates.name: Zinc deficiency dermatitis
support_spans: Plasma zinc was at the lower end of normal (72 μg/dL; reference range 70–120 μg/dL)
candidates.why: The low-normal plasma zinc level could contribute to dermatitis, although it is not definitively low.

candidates.name: Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris
support_spans: well‐defined hyperpigmented, hyperkeratotic plaques with thick adherent scales and a peripheral rim of erythema
candidates.why: The presence of hyperkeratotic plaques with thick adherent scales is consistent with Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be overlooked due to its rarity and similarity in presentation to other skin conditions.

candidates.name: Sjögren's Syndrome
contradict_spans: negative hepatitis C and B serologies
candidates.why: The combination of pruritic plaques and elevated thyroid-stimulating hormone levels could suggest an autoimmune component, such as Sjögren's Syndrome.
candidates.protected_reason: Sjögren's Syndrome can be difficult to diagnose due to its varied presentation and the need for specific diagnostic criteria.

candidates.name: Zinc Deficiency
support_spans: plasma zinc was at the lower end of normal (72 μg/dL; reference range 70–120 μg/dL)
contradict_spans: normal levels of aspartate and alanine aminotransferases
candidates.why: The low plasma zinc level could contribute to the patient's skin symptoms, as zinc deficiency can cause skin lesions and impaired wound healing.
candidates.protected_reason: Zinc deficiency may be underdiagnosed due to its nonspecific symptoms and the need for laboratory confirmation.

rejected.label: Zinc deficiency dermatitis
